name: KeBTAH Rising Firefly Portal
tag: Brings Nile Valley and Dogon teachings into one archive, calendar and study space.

scenarios.title: Build a personal study path
scenarios.ask: Give me a {weeks}-week study path on {focus}, about {mins} a day.
steps: Archive
Pulled {=12 + focus * 8} entries matched to your focus, each with its source listed.
Planner
Ordered them from core ideas, such as the principle of Maat, to more detailed readings.
Calendar
Placed {=weeks * 5} study sessions on weekdays and left weekends for review.
Reflection
Added a short journal prompt to the end of each week.
followups: Is the Dogon material settled history?
Not all of it. Some 20th-century accounts of Dogon cosmology have been questioned by later researchers. The portal labels each entry with its source and flags readings that are debated.
What does Maat mean in the portal?
The portal presents Maat as the ancient Egyptian idea of truth, balance and right order, with readings from primary texts in translation.
Yes. Change the minutes per day and the calendar re-spreads the remaining sessions.

scenarios.title: Digitize a community collection
scenarios.ask: Our group has {items} {kind} to preserve and {vols} volunteers. Plan the archive work.
steps: Intake
Created an intake form for each item: who gave it, where it came from and any permissions.
Tagger
Suggested tags for people, places and themes so items can be found later.
Transcriber
Drafts text for documents and recordings for a volunteer to check.
Planner
Split {items} items across {vols} volunteers at about 3 hours a week each.
followups: You choose per item: private to the group, shared with members, or public. Families can ask to keep items private.
Each recording needs listening, a checked transcript and consent notes, so it takes about three times the effort of a photo.

scenarios.title: Plan study circles by season
scenarios.ask: Schedule study circles for {size} people, {per} meetings in each of the three seasons of the ancient Egyptian year.
steps: Calendar
Showed the civil year's three seasons, Akhet, Peret and Shemu, each four months of 30 days.
Scheduler
Placed {=per * 3} meetings across the year and sent invites.
Archive
Attached one reading and one discussion question to each meeting.
Groups
Split the circle into {=ceil(size / 8)} discussion group(s) of up to 8.
followups: The calendar view also shows the five added days at the end of the civil year, which made 365 days in total.
Yes. Suggestions go to the circle leader for approval before they join the archive.
